name: traceroute
description: Shows the route packets take to a host, hop by hop, revealing where connections slow down or die.

flags.description: Do not resolve hop IPs to names (much faster).
Use ICMP echoes instead of UDP (some paths treat UDP differently).
Use TCP SYN packets — often passes firewalls that block UDP/ICMP.

examples.explanation: Each line is one router on the path with its round-trip time. The first hop is your own gateway.
TCP-based tracing to port 443 — the way to trace when UDP probes are filtered.

about: traceroute exploits the IP TTL field: it sends packets with TTL 1, 2, 3...; each router that decrements TTL to zero returns an ICMP Time Exceeded message, identifying itself. Routers may rate-limit these replies, showing *** for hops that are actually fine. mtr combines traceroute with continuous statistics.
useCases: Find where traffic stops or slows.
Identify the ISP or backbone segment causing problems.
mistakes: Treating *** hops as failures — many routers simply deprioritize TTL-exceeded replies.
Expecting symmetric paths: the return route may differ.
distroNotes: traceroute is from the traceroute package. tracepath (iputils) needs no root and auto-detects MTU; Windows calls it tracert.
